skipTitle: Skip the tone and read this page first if:
skip: The phone was under water, not only splashed.
The phone does not turn on, or the screen does not respond.
The phone is hot, or the battery looks swollen.
The liquid was salt water, soap, juice, or another sugary liquid.
skipNote: In these cases, power the phone off, keep it unplugged, dry it in airflow, and ask the maker or a repair shop. The tone does not reach the inside of the phone.
stepsTitle: What to do if your phone gets wet, in order

steps.t: Take the phone out of the water. If it was submerged, turn the phone off.
Do not plug in a cable. Do not charge the phone. Wet connector pins can corrode and cause permanent damage.
Take off the case and any accessories.
Wipe the outside with a clean, soft, dry cloth. Do not press hard. Hard pressure can push liquid further in.
Tap the phone gently against your hand with the connector facing down. This removes excess liquid.
Hold the phone with the speaker facing down, or put it speaker side down on a lint-free cloth. Check if water drips out.
Do not use a hair dryer, heat, or compressed air. Do not push a cotton swab, paper towel, or other object into an opening.
Leave the phone in a dry place with some airflow. A fan that blows cool air into the connector can help.
Wait at least 5 hours before you charge with a cable. This is Apple's rule for a wet iPhone. See the details below.
Only if the phone is on, responds normally, and was not submerged: you can try the tone on the home page. It helps with a muffled speaker only.
